title: Verify that pr-ledger.md matches pr-ledger.json (539 stale rows, attribution intact)
body:
## Summary

`scripts/find_overlap.py` reads `docs/research/pr-ledger.md` as its `local-ledger`
overlap corpus. `scripts/verify_pr_reconciliation.py` checks only
`docs/research/pr-ledger.json`. `scripts/reconcile_pr_queue.py` writes both files
but never verifies the committed `.md`. **Nothing in the repository checks that the
two ledgers agree.**

The committed `.md` is currently stale relative to the committed `.json`.

## Result

Base commit `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6
(verified again at submission time against canonical `main`).

- 3028 Markdown rows vs 3028 JSON PRs — no missing or unexpected PR
- the disposition **counts table matches exactly**
- **539 rows (PRs #1365–#3528) disagree**

Attribution is **not** affected: the contributor and disposition cells are
identical in all 539 cases, so recorded credit is intact. The divergence is
confined to the evidence-record column.

## Root cause (539/539, no exceptions)

For every one of the 539, `reconciliation_evidence` in `pr-ledger.json` contains
`docs/research/pr-intake-decisions.json`, and the Markdown row lacks it.

Example, PR #1365:

```text
json  reconciliation_evidence:
      research/community-efficient500-audit/DISPOSITIONS.json
      research/community-efficient2000-audit/DISPOSITIONS.json
      research/community-efficient2500-audit/DISPOSITIONS.json
      research/community-efficient2600-audit/DISPOSITIONS.json
      docs/research/pr-intake-decisions.json
      docs/research/pr-intake-evidence/queue-oct18-20261018.json      (6 records)

md    [Exact-head intake](../../docs/research/pr-intake-evidence/queue-oct18-20261018.json)
                                                                       (1 record)
```

So the intake-queue tooling updates `pr-ledger.json` in place, adding
`pr-intake-decisions.json` to `reconciliation_evidence`, while `pr-ledger.md` is
only written by `reconcile_pr_queue.py`, which is not re-run. The drift is
permanent and grows with every intake round.

## Why it matters, stated honestly

Impact is **bounded and modest**, not a scientific result:

- no change to κ, to `certificates/selected-result.json`, or to any mathematical claim
- **credit and attribution are intact** — the two credit-critical fields agree everywhere
- the real effect is a **weaker/partial overlap signal** for 539 PRs in the exact
  corpus the overlap process depends on, in a repository that documents recurring
  duplicate work

`find_overlap.py` currently reports a `local-ledger` hit with no freshness or
binding information, so a stale ledger is indistinguishable from a current one.

## The verifier

`scripts/verify_pr_ledger_markdown.py` re-derives the Markdown projection that
`reconcile_pr_queue.py` (lines 363–371) emits — disposition counts plus one row per
PR with number, contributor, disposition and ordered evidence records — and reports
a bounded set of differences instead of a bare boolean.

```sh
python3 scripts/verify_pr_ledger_markdown.py           # FAIL, exit 1 (539 differences)
python3 scripts/verify_pr_ledger_markdown.py --json    # full structured report
python3 -B tests/test_verify_pr_ledger_markdown.py      # 13 tests, OK
python3 -B tests/test_research_assignment.py            # OK (skipped=2)
python3 -B tests/test_research_coordination.py          # OK
```

13 tests: one positive fixture plus eight failure controls (dropped evidence
record, disposition drift, attribution drift, missing row, count drift, duplicate
row, absent counts table, JSON `counts` self-drift), one evidence dedup/ordering
control and one repository-shape assertion that does not hard-code the current
(known-stale) state.

The derivation is corroborated by 2489 of 3028 rows matching it exactly.

## What I deliberately did **not** do

I did **not** regenerate `pr-ledger.md`. `python3 scripts/reconcile_pr_queue.py`
would rewrite it, but that rewrites a tracked evidence artifact and is a
maintainer decision — and it is not clear that regenerating is even the intended
fix (see open questions). I also did **not** wire the verifier into
`scripts/verify_pr_reconciliation.py`, because
[#3686](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3686) currently
modifies that file; a maintainer can decide the integration point.

If regenerating is intended, the one-line fix is:

```sh
python3 scripts/reconcile_pr_queue.py && python3 scripts/verify_pr_ledger_markdown.py
```

## Overlap check

Live checks were completed for this PR (authenticated REST + GraphQL):

- open PR titles/bodies searched for ledger-binding work
- Discussions [#1163](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163)
  and [#1166](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166)
  scanned (the last 60 comments of each; #1166 holds 574 in total)

**Adjacent but not duplicative:**
[#3686](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3686)
("Preserve optional intake metadata in ledger verification", by @roger-sato) fixes a
`KeyError: 'closure'` crash in the JSON-side checker for 24 intake decisions. It is
the same ledger family and the same canonical base, and it explicitly cites
PR1365 — one of the 539 rows above. It does **not** compare the Markdown ledger to
the JSON ledger. Its diff touches `scripts/verify_pr_reconciliation.py` and
`tests/test_pr_reconciliation.py`; this PR adds only new files, so there is no
conflict.

## Predecessor credit

- [@roife](https://github.com/roife) — [#704](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/704),
  the original review-ledger metadata binding and its rejection controls
- Douglas R. Colkitt — the reconciliation infrastructure (`reconcile_pr_queue.py`,
  `verify_pr_reconciliation.py`)
- [@Dennis](https://github.com/dennis) / @antunishdPursuit —
  [#2026](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2026) and
  [#2859](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2859), historical replay maintenance
- [#2624](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2624) — precedent for
  fixing a stale blocker in a *generated* ledger
- @roger-sato — [#3686](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3686),
  whose failure analysis surfaced the same ledger family

I found no prior work binding `pr-ledger.md` to `pr-ledger.json`. I dropped an
earlier candidate (auditing `selected-result.json` hash bindings) because
`scripts/verify_selected_result.py` already covers it.

## Remaining obligations / not claimed

- I did **not** determine whether the `.md`/`.json` divergence is intentional or a
  bug. A reviewer should decide that before regenerating.
- I did **not** run any cold replay, Lean check, or arithmetic. This is an
  attribution/coverage binding check only; it establishes nothing about κ.
- The derivation reproduces my reading of `reconcile_pr_queue.py:363-371`. The
  2489 exact row matches corroborate it, but a second reader is welcome.
- Only the last 60 comments of each discussion were scanned, not all 574.
- No live GitHub PR state was audited; that is `verify_pr_reconciliation.py`'s job.

## Open next questions

1. **Is the divergence intentional?** If `pr-ledger.md` is meant to be a frozen
   human snapshot rather than a projection of the JSON, the right fix is to state
   that contract and stop emitting both from the same inputs.
2. **Which tool appends `pr-intake-decisions.json` to `reconciliation_evidence`?**
   Closing the loop at the *writer* is more robust than checking at the reader.
3. **Should `find_overlap.py` report ledger freshness?** It can currently be
   pointed at a stale ledger with no signal.

```json
{
  "schema": "integer-mult-coordination/v1",
  "kind": "FINDING",
  "task": "overlap-receipt",
  "scope": "Check pr-ledger.md, the find_overlap.py local-ledger corpus, against pr-ledger.json: 539 stale rows, attribution intact",
  "base": "20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90",
  "expiry": null,
  "artifact": "https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3695"
}
```
